title: Accomplishments
raw_text:
Accomplishments
Education - Strengthening School Safety
• Chaired the 2013 House Select Committee for School Safety, formed after the 2012 Sandy Hook tragedy, to strengthen school security across Pennsylvania.
• Led bipartisan efforts through public hearings with school officials, law enforcement and parents, delivering a report recommending frequent intruder drills, local safety committees and “choke point” campus designs.
• Co-authored
House Bill 178
, unanimously passed by the House and enacted as
Act 55 of 2017
, requiring annual school security drills for threats like armed intruders. By replacing one monthly fire drill, this law ensures flexibility and preparedness, safeguarding students and staff statewide.
Seniors – Leading During Pandemic Governance - COVID-19
• Directed the House Aging and Older Adult Services Committee, appointed in January 2020, to protect Pennsylvania’s seniors during the COVID-19 pandemic as the first committee to resume work in Harrisburg.
• Brought Health Secretary Rachel Levine before six public hearings in 2020 to demand accountability, challenging the secretary’s unprecedented authority – surpassing even the governor’s – to shut down businesses, schools and places of worship, restricting citizens’ lives.
• Oversaw a March 2021 hearing on vaccination distribution for the state’s most vulnerable seniors and co-authored letters with House Majority Leader Kerry Benninghoff to press for transparency on regulatory suspensions.
• Advanced
House Bills 397
,
398
,
399
and
400
to combat elder abuse, ensuring robust support through programs like prescription drug assistance and the Property Tax and Rent Rebate Program with bipartisan leadership.
HomeOwners - Restructuring Private Road Maintenance
• Authored
House Bill 523
, enacted as
Act 75 of 2021
, to support homeowners by reforming the Private Road Act.
• The law requires property owners to share private road maintenance costs when no agreement exists, addressing banking regulations that blocked federally backed mortgages.
• This reform ensures passable roads and easier home financing, benefiting Pennsylvanians, especially in rural areas.
Reducing Redundant Regulation - Reforming Government for the People
• Championed government efficiency by authoring
House Bills 754
and
755
to streamline bottled water regulation, ensuring better service for Pennsylvania’s citizens.
• Led efforts to consolidate oversight under the Department of Agriculture, reducing duplicative regulations while maintaining safety standards.
• Secured broad bipartisan support in the House, with both bills earning unanimous approval from the House Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee before advancing to the Senate.
• This initiative reflects a commitment to collaborative, common-sense reforms that simplify government processes for businesses and residents,
Appropriations – Budget
• Served on the Pennsylvania House of Representatives Appropriations Committee for six and a half years, playing a pivotal role in scrutinizing and shaping the state's annual budget.
• Participated extensively in budget hearings, rigorously questioning administration officials on spending priorities and accountability for taxpayer dollars.
• Helped determine funding levels and influenced policy across critical areas including education, transportation, public safety, environmental protection, agriculture and economic development.
• Widely regarded as a serious, detail-oriented and reliable legislator who works effectively across the aisle within the chamber to promote responsible spending and fiscal discipline, ensuring efficient use of resources for the benefit of all Pennsylvanians.

title: Coleman, Day to Host Hard-to-Read License Plate Event on Aug. 27
raw_text:
Coleman, Day to Host Hard-to-Read License Plate Event on Aug. 27
August 18, 2026
MACUNGIE — State Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R-16) and state Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) will partner with the Lehigh County Sheriff’s Office, the Pennsylvania State Police and Lower Macungie Township to host a
hard-to-read license plate event on Thursday, Aug. 27, at the Lower Macungie Community Center, 3450 Brookside Dr., Macungie, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.
“Assisting with PennDOT issues is one of the most utilized services that my office provides,” Coleman said. “I am pleased to partner with Rep. Gary Day to offer this license plate replacement event to help streamline the process for my constituents.”
“Vehicle owners can have their peeling, fading or unreadable plates inspected on-site and get immediate help filing the paperwork for a free replacement,” said Day. “Replacing damaged plates ensures law enforcement can identify vehicles while saving drivers from costly fines and inspection failures.”
People can sign up for the event at
senatorcoleman.com/events
. Questions about the event or registration can be directed to Day’s office at 610-965-9933 or Coleman’s office at 484-861-4964.

East Penn School District - $449,924.
•
Northern Lehigh School District - $173,074.

Northwestern Lehigh School District - $185,547.

Parkland School District - $533,650.

title: Day Invites Local Students to Enter ‘State Representative for a Day’ Essay Contest
raw_text:
Day Invites Local Students to Enter ‘State Representative for a Day’ Essay Contest
August 12, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) is inviting high school students throughout the 187th Legislative District to participate in his “State Representative for a Day” essay contest.
The contest is open to students in grades 9-12. Participants are asked to identify a real-world issue they believe should be addressed by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives and propose a practical solution.
“Young people bring valuable perspectives to the issues facing our communities and Commonwealth,” Day said. “This contest will give students an opportunity to think critically about public policy, develop a realistic solution and learn how ideas can become laws. I look forward to reading their proposals.”
A panel of judges, including Day, will select three winning essays. Each winner will be invited to Harrisburg to shadow Day for a day, tour the state Capitol, and learn more about the legislative process and the responsibilities of a state representative.
Essays must be submitted by Wednesday, Sept. 30, to hbortz@pahousegop.com. Submissions should include the student’s name, grade, school and contact information. Questions about the contest may be directed to Day’s district office at 610-965-9933.
The 187th Legislative District includes the boroughs of Alburtis and Macungie, as well as Heidelberg, Lower Macungie, Lynn, Washington and Weisenberg townships and portions of Upper Macungie Township.

title: Rep. Day: House Bill 1042 Opposition Was Necessary
raw_text:
Rep. Day: House Bill 1042 Opposition Was Necessary
July 27, 2026
HARRISBURG – Following his vote against
House Bill 1042
, Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) issued this statement:
“Although the Pennsylvania Supreme Court’s July 24 deadline has now passed, voting against the revised House Bill 1042 when House Democrats forced a vote on July 23 was necessary. The previous version, which would have earned my wholehearted support, established a clear mandatory minimum sentence for second-degree murder while allowing sentences to reflect an offender’s actual level of participation and culpability.
“Instead of advancing that responsible compromise to the governor, House Democrats replaced it with a last-minute rewrite containing inadequate sentencing provisions, opportunities for forum shopping and unrelated medical-release language with serious loopholes for convicted murderers and sex offenders.
“It is therefore disingenuous to blame those who voted ‘no’ for the missed deadline or claim that their votes endangered public safety. The deadline could have been met by restoring and passing the previous version of House Bill 1042. House Democrats chose instead to force a vote on deeply flawed legislation.
“A looming deadline could not justify abandoning accountability, weakening protections for victims or potentially making it easier for violent offenders to obtain release.”
Representative Gary Day

title: Rep. Day: 2026-27 State Budget Statement
raw_text:
Rep. Day: 2026-27 State Budget Statement
July 14, 2026
HARRISBURG – Following the passage of the 2026-27 state budget, Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) issued the following statement:
“No budget is perfect, but this one reflects the priorities of the people I represent. I’m glad it wasn’t significantly delayed like last year’s budget, which meant people who depend on the budget’s funding weren’t left in limbo for months.
“It boosts PreK-12 education funding by nearly $680 million and ensures every Pennsylvania school district, including those in the 187th District, will see an increase in funding for the coming school year. We’re also preserving the Educational Improvement Tax Credit and Opportunity Scholarship Tax Credit programs, which give families real choices in their children’s education. And it continues necessary support for career and technical education centers by providing an additional $10 million to address waitlists for students interested in pursuing their education at these centers.
“This budget also remembers those who have contributed to our communities. It includes a pension cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for retired municipal police officers and firefighters, many of whom have not received a COLA in more than 20 years. A COLA will also be provided to retired public servants, including teachers, who retired before significant pension changes were implemented in 2001. These are people who dedicated their careers to serving our communities, and it’s long past time they received some relief. There is also increased funding to improve services and strengthen support for our older adults and senior citizens.
“Additionally, this agreement includes $775 million for shovel-ready rural road and bridge projects – $500 million this fiscal year and $275 million next fiscal year – to repair state-owned roads across Pennsylvania beginning this construction season.
“These things matter here at home, whether it’s safer roads, better schools, giving students a path into skilled trades or ensuring our older neighbors are supported wherever they live. This budget shows what’s possible when we prioritize our communities without asking families and businesses to pay more.”

title: Day Announces Grant for Upper Macungie Park Plan
raw_text:
Day Announces Grant for Upper Macungie Park Plan
May 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today announced he helped secure a $90,140 Local Share Account (LSA) grant from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) for the Lone Lane Park Master Plan Project in Upper Macungie Township.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“Outdoor recreation is hugely popular in the Lehigh Valley, especially during warmer months when families want to get outside and enjoy our parks,” Day said. “Lone Lane Park offers tremendous potential, but its current layout creates real access challenges for many residents. This grant funding will help develop a smart, practical plan to make the park fully accessible so everyone – seniors, families with young children and individuals with disabilities – can enjoy it safely and comfortably.”
The park is the second most used for programming and community events but has accessibility and connectivity limitations. There is only one vehicular access point, no clear pedestrian access points and routes to park amenities are not accessible. The plan will evaluate the park directly and a nearby northern parcel to see if it can be connected to increase park amenities.

Day, Coleman Partner to Bring New Community Sign to Heidelberg Township
May 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) and Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R-Lehigh/Bucks) today announced they secured a $43,000 Local Share Account (LSA) grant from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) to purchase a new outdoor community sign for Heidelberg Township.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“Even in this age of social media, important local information can still get missed,” Day said. “This new digital sign at Heidelberg will help ensure our residents – and those just traveling through – stay informed about key community news, events, and public safety updates. It’s a simple, effective way to improve transparency and keep everyone connected”
“I’m proud to join Representative Day in announcing this state grant sought by Heidelberg Township for a new digital sign at the municipal building,” Coleman said. “The township will soon be able to share upcoming event, traffic, safety and other important messages with area residents quickly and efficiently.”
The funding will pay for the purchase and installation of a digital municipal sign that will allow the township to instantly share multiple messages, such as meeting dates, road closures, public safety alerts, volunteer opportunities and community events without delay or limitations of the current manual sign.

Day Announces Grants for 187th District Fire, EMS Companies
February 17, 2026
MACUNGIE – State Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) announced today that six fire and emergency medical services (EMS) companies in the 187th Legislative District were collectively awarded more than $96,000 in funding support through the 2025-26 Pennsylvania Fire Company and Emergency Medical Services Grant Program.
“I am truly grateful for the unwavering dedication and hard work of our first responders. Their service is vital to safeguarding families and communities across the 187th District,” said Day. “This grant program delivers essential funding for smaller projects that support our fire and ambulance personnel. By easing the burden of fundraising, it allows these brave men and women to focus on what they do best: Protect and assist residents in times of need. I am proud to support our first responders and will continue advocating for the resources they need to carry out their life-saving mission.”
Projects eligible for funding include construction or renovation of a fire or ambulance company facility, purchase or repair of equipment, training, recruitment and retention, public education about fire safety, or reduction of existing debt. The funding amounts are contingent on the recipients filing their grant agreements with the Office of the State Fire Commissioner.

•	Community Fire Company of New Tripoli – $13,000.

•	Lower Macungie Fire Department – $28,136.55.

title: Day Issues 2025-26 State Budget Statement
raw_text:
Day Issues 2025-26 State Budget Statement
November 13, 2025
HARRISBURG
– Following the passage of the 2025-26 state budget, Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) issued this statement:
“I couldn’t support parts of the budget because the General Appropriations bill spends more than the annual revenues our state collects from taxpayers. While there are things I don’t like about this agreement, I voted for several pieces of it that represent a commitment to core principles that put Pennsylvanians first.
“I support parts of the budget agreement that reassert the authority of the General Assembly by repealing, through statute, Wolf Administration regulations that forced Pennsylvania into the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative. This action restores legislative oversight, protects and helps in creating family-sustaining energy jobs, avoids what would have been a 30% increase in energy bills by 2030 and revitalizes our Commonwealth’s energy industry to help ensure a reliable energy grid. The agreement also expands expedited permitting for business development, something that will not only help our energy industry, but also spur economic growth throughout our Commonwealth.
“I also support the significant strides portions of this budget make to expand opportunity and reform welfare. We’re returning taxpayer money directly to low- to moderate-income working Pennsylvanians and their families through a new tax credit program that helps workers keep more of what they earn. And we’re reinforcing benefit integrity to ensure those who receive public assistance are those who truly need it. Reducing waste, fraud and abuse in our state’s public health programs will not only help rein in out-of-control spending, but it will also reduce health care costs for everyone.
“While I don’t agree with how much this budget spends, we were able to prevent tax hikes, avoid taking money out of the Rainy Day Fund and preserve planned tax reductions that will make Pennsylvania more competitive with other states.”

Day: Efforts to Address 187th District Traffic Concerns Continue
September 18, 2025
MACUNGIE – State Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) provided an update regarding the ongoing efforts to address traffic congestion issues plaguing an area of the 187th Legislative District.
“I recently met with representatives of Dorney Park/Six Flags and during that meeting, park officials expressed their interest in finding a solution and shared with me their ideas about improvements to make Dorney Park more easily accessible and safe,” said Day.
Many residents have reached out to Day with concerns about traffic congestion, particularly in the area of Hamilton Boulevard and Brookside Road, as well as along the traffic corridor containing U.S. Route 222, Interstate 78 and State Route 309. After surveying the 187th District during the first few months of his term, Day identified that area as the top traffic problem in the district.
Having a good relationship with the professionals of Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) District 5, Day is committed to working with them, local officials and interested parties to find and pursue long-term solutions.
“I intend to work collaboratively with them to advocate for transportation infrastructure that will handle the needs of our area well into the future,” Day said.

Day: Addressing Local Traffic Congestion is My Transportation Priority
August 6, 2025
MACUNGIE – State Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today identified the ongoing traffic congestion issues plaguing a portion of the 187th Legislative District as his transportation priority in the district and reaffirmed his commitment to working with state and local officials to identify and pursue long-term solutions.
“Many residents have reached out to me with concerns about traffic congestion, particularly in the area of Hamilton Boulevard and Brookside Road, as well as along the traffic corridor containing U.S. Route 222, Interstate 78 and State Route 309 near Dorney Park,” said Day. “These are concerns I share as I’ve driven these roads myself and experienced the same delays and backups.”
Day has met with representatives of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) and has had conversations with local officials and involved parties about the issue, with the goal being to work collaboratively to move toward effective, long-term improvements.
“This area contains the intersection of state, federal and local roadways,” Day said. “We have traffic from Dorney Park, retail development, the Pennsylvania Turnpike and constituent residences, all converging in this area. I’m working to create a transportation infrastructure plan to handle the traffic volume created by all of these interested parties.
“I want residents to know their voices are being heard. I’ve taken their concerns directly to PennDOT and local leaders, and I will continue advocating for the transportation needs of our community.”

title: Coleman, Day Announce $150,000 in Grants for Lehigh County
raw_text:
Coleman, Day Announce $150,000 in Grants for Lehigh County
May 22, 2025
HARRISBURG
–
Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R-16)
and
Rep. Gary Day (R-187)
today announced that two townships in Lehigh County received state grants totaling nearly $150,000 from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA). The projects will improve community safety and resources.
Heidelberg Township was awarded more than $122,000 to upgrade the stadium lighting at the Northwestern Lehigh Tiger Stadium. The existing light fixtures from 1994 would be upgraded to LED fixtures. Electrical panels, wiring and controls will be added.
“The stadium is not just a place to play football, hockey and soccer. It’s also a place for people to gather, a fixture in the community,” Coleman said. “It’s important to complete work that will help the stadium continue to be an asset to the area.”
“I am proud to support important local projects that strengthen our community’s health and togetherness. Upgrading critical CPR equipment for the Macungie Ambulance Corps ensures our first responders have the reliable tools they need to save lives and provide the highest level of care,” said Day. Meanwhile, improving the lighting at Northwestern Lehigh Tiger Stadium enhances safety and visibility for athletes and spectators alike, while also reflecting a commitment to sustainability. These investments will have a meaningful, positive impact on both Lower Macungie and Heidelberg Township, and I’m glad to see them funded.”
Lower Macungie Township received nearly $27,500 to purchase CPR equipment for the local emergency medical services. The Macungie Ambulance Corps operates five ambulances, each of which has a mechanical CPR device. Three of the devices were purchased recently, but the other two are 12 years old and have exceeded the manufacturer’s expected lifespan by four years. The grant would be used to purchase two new devices.
“The Macungie Ambulance Corps has proven how well it cares for equipment, keeping it functional for 150% of its anticipated useful life. Even with that diligence, equipment doesn’t last forever,” Coleman said. “This grant will enable the ambulance corps to serve our community without fear of imminent equipment failure.”
The grants were awarded by the
Commonwealth Financing Authority
through its
Local Share Account Program
, which funds projects concerning the public interest, community improvement and economic development using gaming money generated by casinos.

title: Day Questions Democrats’ Rush to Pass Complex Recreational Marijuana Bill
raw_text:
Day Questions Democrats’ Rush to Pass Complex Recreational Marijuana Bill
May 6, 2025
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today questioned why House Democrats are rushing a complex, 173-page bill to legalize adult-use recreational marijuana in Pennsylvania, without any hearings or input from legislators or the public.
“When I look at this bill, it’s just so expansive, and we’ve only just gotten to see the language of the bill,” said Day, who noted he and his House Health Committee colleagues were given about an hour to ask questions about the bill before it was voted out of committee Monday. “The role of the minority party is to help improve upon the legislation, working together with the majority party, particularly during the committee consideration process. By moving this bill as it was by House Democrats, we’re bypassing that vital part of the process.”
House Democrats scheduled a non-voting session day on Sunday, May 4, that allowed the marijuana legislation,
House Bill 1200
, to be introduced and referred to the House Health Committee, setting up Monday’s committee vote.
“This is such an important endeavor that we’re doing, that we’re deciding for Pennsylvanians. I know there are more stops for this bill during the legislative process – getting the input of the Senate, getting the input of the governor – but it’s important that we don’t skip this step. Have a hearing for this proposal. Put this initiative on public display and let the people have input. All that can do is make your plan better,” Day urged.
In addition to legalizing adult-use recreational marijuana, the bill also seeks to address expungement of prior “minor” marijuana offenses, reinvestment of funds generated by the sale and taxation of marijuana in communities the bill identifies as having been “disproportionately harmed by the war on drugs,” and implementing public health protections. The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board would be given oversight of a new state store system from which marijuana products could be purchased by the public.
“Plain and simple, this bill, and the process by which it is being advanced by the House Democrats, makes all Pennsylvanians less safe,” said Day.

title: Day Questions Secrecy About Allentown NIZ Report
raw_text:
Day Questions Secrecy About Allentown NIZ Report
April 1, 2025
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today questioned why a Legislative Budget and Finance Committee (LBFC) report about the Allentown Neighborhood Improvement Zone (NIZ) will be kept confidential.
"The growth in Allentown has been extraordinary, but it's baffling that the details of this report remain hidden," said Day. "All of us in the Lehigh Valley should expect to know what it contains, whatever the results."
The Legislative Budget and Finance Committee, a bipartisan panel of state lawmakers, at its March 24 meeting, considered a motion to release the interim report to the public, but the vote on the motion was tied, preventing the report from being released. The committee’s six Republican members voted to release the report, while the six Democrat members opposed the report’s release.
LBFC reports offer recommendations to the Legislature aimed at eliminating unnecessary expenditures; promoting effectiveness and efficiency in government; and assuring taxpayer dollars are being expended in accordance with legislative intent and law.
The Allentown NIZ, which has seen more than $500 million invested within the zone during the past decade, has come under increased scrutiny for a lack of transparency about how it operates and those overseeing it locally. The improvement zone designation allows nearly all state tax revenues generated by the new development in the zone to be used by those in the zone to pay off debt of the new development.
"The Lehigh Valley is owed transparency, yet the vote to hide the NIZ report denies it,” Day said. “Our institutions must trust the people just as we, the people, trust our institutions. I don't understand... the question everybody should be asking about this is what are the Democrats trying to hide."

title: Day Announces Grants for Local Fire, EMS Departments
raw_text:
Day Announces Grants for Local Fire, EMS Departments
February 14, 2025
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today is celebrating that more than $175,000 was awarded to fire and emergency medical services (EMS) companies in the 187th Legislative District through the 2024-25 Pennsylvania Fire Company and Emergency Medical Services Grant Program.
“This is fantastic news for the dedicated first responders in the 187th Legislative District,” said Day. “Our local fire and EMS companies are the backbone of community safety, and this funding will provide vital support to the brave men and women who risk their lives to protect ours.”
Projects eligible for funding include construction or renovation of a fire or ambulance company facility, purchase or repair of equipment, training, or reduction of existing debt. The ongoing funding program was created by the General Assembly. All grants are generated from slot machine gaming proceeds, not General Fund tax revenue.
The local grants are as follows:
•
Community Fire Company of New Tripoli - $15,461.31.
•
Emmaus Borough EMS - $14,732.
•
Emmaus Fire Department - $15,461.31.
•
Fogelsville Volunteer Fire Company - $13,955.06.
•
Good Will Fire Company No. 1 of Trexlertown - 16,106.84.
•
Goodwill Fire Company No. 1 Inc. of Germansville - $15,030.95.
•
Lower Macungie Fire Department - $28,322.02.
•
Lynnport Community Fire Company No. 1 - $13,955.06.
•
Macungie Ambulance Corps - $15,000.
•
Star Hose Company No. 1 - $13,739.88.
•
Weisenberg Volunteer Fire Department - 14,170.24.
The program is administered by the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency with the application process handled through the Office of the State Fire Commissioner (OSFC). All companies that apply and meet requirements outlined by OSFC receive funding. Companies must file a grant agreement with OSFC to receive their grants.
The 187th Legislative District includes Macungie and Alburtis boroughs, and the townships of Upper Macungie (in part), Lower Macungie, Weisenberg, Lynn, Heidelberg and Washington.

title: Day Responds to Governor’s Budget Proposal
raw_text:
Day Responds to Governor’s Budget Proposal
February 4, 2025
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) attended a joint session of the General Assembly at which Gov. Josh Shapiro presented his budget proposal for the 2025-26 fiscal year. Day issued the following statement in response to the governor’s plan:
“Gov. Shapiro has outlined a budget that includes a 7.5% increase in spending, while revenue collections are only projected to grow by 2.5%. At $51.47 billion, this budget would deplete our state’s surplus of $2.89 billion by the end of this fiscal year and would also require drawing from our Rainy Day Fund. While we understand the governor’s aspirations for Pennsylvania, this proposal places significant pressure on future budgets and fiscal sustainability.
“There are several aspects of the proposal that I support, including funding for firefighters, state police cadets, Pre-K programs, and Career and Technical Education (CTE) schools. These are all important initiatives that I believe will benefit our communities. However, we must also recognize the long-term implications of this budget and take a closer look at its overall impact.
“Right now, this budget appears to be more of a wish list, and while it includes valuable investments, we must also ensure that we remain focused on the taxpayers of Pennsylvania. The proposed spending is substantial, and we must be cautious not to grow government faster than the private sector can sustain. Our priority must be to foster an environment where taxpayers and private sector jobs thrive.
“It’s time for legislators to thoroughly review this budget proposal, with the best interests of taxpayers in mind. We must make fiscally responsible decisions to ensure that the tax burden remains low and that future generations are not burdened by unsustainable spending.”
The governor’s address is just the beginning of the annual state budget process. The House Appropriations Committee will conduct a series of hearings starting Tuesday, Feb. 18, to examine the details of the governor’s plan and how state departments and agencies are spending their funding. The General Assembly and governor face a June 30 deadline to finalize the budget.
Representative Gary Day
187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Day Takes Oath of Office
raw_text:
Day Takes Oath of Office
January 9, 2025
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) took the oath of office Tuesday to begin his term in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives. Day was elected in November to serve a two-year term representing the 187th Legislative District.
“I am deeply humbled and incredibly grateful for the opportunity to serve the residents of the 187th District. It is an honor to represent such a hardworking community,” said Day. “I look forward to working alongside my colleagues to create positive change and strengthen the future of Pennsylvania, while ensuring that the families of the Lehigh Valley continue to thrive and prosper.”
Day previously represented the 187th District from 2008-22. During his tenure, he built a strong conservative voting record and passed key legislation benefiting homeowners and military personnel. Now back in office, Day is committed to addressing the priorities of his constituents, including promoting economic growth, combating inflation, ensuring children’s safety in schools, and protecting the freedoms of every resident.
The 187th Legislative District includes Macungie and Alburtis boroughs, and the townships of Upper Macungie (in part), Lower Macungie, Weisenberg, Lynn, Heidelberg and Washington.
